about: The website's longer description of each app (the home page tiles and app sections). Keys are app ids from static/suite/suite-apps.json; every app there needs an entry here. The short one-line 'what' in suite-apps.json is for the Farm Apps menu. 'in_development' lists apps being built that aren't in the suite list yet: they get a tile on the home page (tagged In development, with Get notified) and nothing else. Move one into suite-apps.json when it opens. "price_from" is the lowest monthly subscription price, shown on the tiles only when config.SHOW_PRICES is True (after billing exists). "shot_alt" describes the app's computer and phone pictures (static/shots/<id>-computer.jpg and -phone.jpg) for people who can't see them. An app with a "page" block gets the fuller page (templates/app_full.html): a headline, a sample cut off partway ("sample"), what is free and what comes with a subscription, the steps, then the weekly card and findings. An app without one keeps the shorter page (templates/app.html). Every claim in "free" and "subscription" must match what the app really locks and opens.

herd-planner.question: Which calves do I sell, which heifers do I keep, and how fast can my herd grow?
points: Prices every animal at your own sale barn from live USDA auction reports, with a range tested on sales the model never saw
Keep or sell: weighs selling now against feeding on, and what a heifer is worth over her working life
Plans your herd size: runs 1,000 possible futures to find how many heifers to keep to reach your goal on the grass you have
Records that work at the chute, from weights to calving and health, even with no signal
herd-planner.note: Keep your herd records and see your barn's prices. The first visit can take a minute to wake up.
herd-planner.shot_alt: Herd Planner on a computer and a phone, showing a demo ranch's answer: keeping a 367 lb steer calf for 120 days is worth about $204 more than selling today, with the costs of keeping and what each length of keeping is worth.

page.headline: Know what your herd is worth, and what to do about it
page.sub: Which calves to sell, which heifers to keep, how fast the herd can grow, and a page your banker can read. From your own records and your own sale barn's prices.
page.offer: Opening by invite: join the waitlist on the app's first screen. With an account, everything is open for your first 30 days. The first visit can take a minute to wake up.

sample.title: A Report for Your Lender
sample.lead: When the bank asks for your cattle numbers, the page is already made, from the records you keep anyway.
points: Head and value by kind, calves and the breeding herd apart
Cows at their cull price, beside your own figure for them
A likely range on the total, and what changed since January
A PDF to print, or emailed to your banker from the app
sample.alt: The first page of a sample lender report for a made-up ranch, marked as a demo: cattle on hand by kind with head, average weight and value, then the breeding herd.
sample.more: The sample goes on: what changed since January, the year's sales, and every animal by tag.
sample.caption: A sample with made-up cattle. Yours is made from your own records and priced from USDA sale reports. It is not an appraisal.

page.free_note: Always, for any size of herd

Your own spreadsheet in, whatever its columns are called, and your herd back out any time
Weigh days straight from the scale, and weights at the chute with no signal
Your barn's prices this week, and a price check for any one animal you describe
Keep-or-sell and herd-growth answers for numbers you type in
Sales recorded the way the settlement sheet reads, added up for your books
page.subscription_note: Everything in Free, worked out for your own herd

A herd growth plan that starts from your real cows, heifers and records
Which head to sell first when grass is short, and what your cull cows would bring
Each sale set beside cattle like yours at the same sale
Whether weaning and holding pays for your calf crop
A report for your lender, as a PDF you can print or email

Every animal, this week, at your barn
For any animal, with the reasons
page.weekly_title: Free on This Site Every Week
page.weekly_text: Each Friday we publish what a 550 lb steer brought at the sale barn nearest one farm county, with the range 8 in 10 sales landed in, and whether the month usually pays to wait.
page.weekly_note: Herd Planner does this for every animal you own, at the barn you sell at.

corn-yield-predictor.question: What will this county's corn and soybeans yield, and why?
corn-yield-predictor.audience: For corn and soybean growers and advisers
points: Predicts county corn and soybean yields from 26 seasons of USDA yields, NASA daily weather, soil ratings and irrigation
Tested the hard way: on whole districts and future years it never saw, and on Iowa after learning only from Nebraska
Maps where the model is strong and where it misses, so you know when to trust it
Shows which weather matters for which crop, and where: August rain decides soybeans, and a long dry spell hurts Nebraska corn but not Iowa's
corn-yield-predictor.note: No account needed. Corn and soybeans, Nebraska and Iowa.
corn-yield-predictor.shot_alt: Yield Predictor on a computer, showing a map of average corn yield by Nebraska county, 2000 to 2025, and on a phone, Hall County's yield history, actual against predicted, with the 80% range around each prediction.

farm-equipment-planner.question: Will this machine pay for itself on my farm?
points: The true cost to own and run a machine, by the ASABE and Iowa State method
Replays your county's real falls since 2000 to price the bushels a bigger machine saves
Buy new, buy used, lease or hire custom, compared across thousands of simulated seasons
Finds the harvest bottleneck: the combine, carts, trucks, pit or dryer
farm-equipment-planner.note: Invite only while we test it: sign up with a Cornerpost invite code. The first visit can take a minute to wake up.
farm-equipment-planner.shot_alt: Farm Equipment Planner on a computer and a phone, comparing ways to get a combine for 1,200 acres of corn in Hall County, Nebraska: hiring custom harvesting costs the least, about $64.58 an acre a year.

grazing-planner.question: How much grass will my pasture grow this season, and how many head can it carry?
grazing-planner.audience: For ranches and anyone renting out grass
points: Forecasts this season's grass for every Nebraska county from satellite estimates and the weather so far, with an 80% range
Head that can graze May to October with enough grass 9 years in 10, and the chance your own herd runs short
Green-up date in spring, and a July 1 and August 1 check: keep, move or sell
Tested season by season on 2011-2025, and against Grass-Cast, the public forecast from USDA and partners
grazing-planner.note: No sign-in needed to try it. Nebraska counties for now; drawing your own pasture comes later.
grazing-planner.shot_alt: Grazing Planner on a computer and a phone, showing the August 1 check for 120 pairs on 2,000 acres of Frontier County, Nebraska native range: keep your 120 pairs; this year's grass is 8% below normal.
